body:
FINAL RECOMMENDATION — MIRRORED DISPLAY + SECOND-DEVICE PRESENTER CONSOLE

Locked MVP assumptions:
- Presenter is account-authenticated and authorized for the deck/session before pairing.
- Anonymous presenter mode is out of MVP; therefore no weak human-code-only ownership path.
- Cloud operator confidentiality/E2EE is not required; TLS plus service-side ACLs protects network confidentiality, while normal privileged service operation remains trusted.
- Cloud reachability is required. Fully offline LAN is not MVP.

Choose this one safe protocol:
1. Public machine loads `https://display.example.com/p/{sid}` and authenticates with a narrow DISPLAY session. It opens outbound `wss://display.example.com/socket`.
2. Account-authorized presenter initiates pairing from the display/session owner flow. Server creates a one-use, 256-bit random, <=120-second pair secret and pairingId. QR is `https://console.example.com/pair#p=<id>&s=<secret>`. This fragment value is a short-lived pairing credential, technically bearer-like only for the one redemption endpoint; the rule “no bearer token in URL” means no durable access/session token in path/query/fragment and no bearer in the WebSocket URL. Reconcile safely by: fragment is never sent in the HTTP request or Referer, pair page has no third-party resources/analytics, JS immediately scrubs URL, redeem requires the already account-authenticated authorized presenter, store only HMAC(secret), atomically consume once, rate-limit, and issue the real session only as `__Host-presenter` Secure HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie. Thus QR possession alone does not confer control and no reusable bearer/access token is URL-carried.
3. Console opens `wss://console.example.com/socket` using that host-only cookie. Upgrade enforces exact Origin and server role. Display and console are separate origins and sockets/BFFs.
4. Server WSS relay is authoritative for commands, revisions, snapshots, receipts and signaling. Optional WebRTC data channel is deferred until telemetry proves the cloud path misses SLOs; WebTransport is deferred. BroadcastChannel may coordinate tabs on one origin/device only and is never a remote transport.
5. Strict server topics: `public.state` -> DISPLAY+PRESENTER; `presenter.private` -> PRESENTER only; `control.commands` <- current PRESENTER only; sanitized `control.receipts` -> PRESENTER; `display.receipts` <- DISPLAY only. The display never receives a private object and cannot request arbitrary topics.
6. Reconnect sends role-scoped `resume(lastSeenRevision,lastAckedCommandId,controllerEpoch)`; server returns contiguous events or authoritative snapshot. Dedupe commandId, compare baseRevision, require monotonic revision and active epoch. Do not blindly replay relative commands.
7. Latency SLOs: cloud WSS send-to-display-applied p50 <=150 ms, p95 <=300 ms, p99 <=750 ms; reconnect-to-snapshot p95 <=2 s when reachable. These are measured product targets, not transport promises.

MVP takeover UX decision:
- One active presenter lease.
- A second console sees “Another presenter is controlling this session” and may request takeover.
- Current console gets a 10-second approve/deny prompt. If it is unreachable, the authenticated deck owner may force takeover after re-authentication (WebAuthn/password/SSO freshness per existing account policy), with an explicit warning. The public display never shows an approval secret and never becomes the default authorization UI.
- Approval or owner force-takeover increments controllerEpoch atomically, closes/revokes the old presenter connection, and all old commands return STALE_CONTROLLER. This balances interruption safety with recovery from a lost phone. Silent last-connection-wins is rejected.

Transport comparison:
- WebSocket — MVP winner. Browser/server bidirectional, mature, outbound TLS/TCP 443 deployment, straightforward central auth/ordering/replay. Constraints: server hop, application schema/reconnect required, browser API cannot originate protocol Ping, bounded queues/backpressure must be implemented. Primary: RFC 6455 https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455 and WHATWG API https://websockets.spec.whatwg.org/ .
- WebRTC data channel — optional later fast path. Ordered/unordered and reliable/partially reliable SCTP over DTLS over ICE/UDP; peer path may reduce relay distance, but needs authenticated signaling, ICE candidate handling, STUN/TURN, connection restart, and server authorization anyway. Directness is not guaranteed: difficult NATs require TURN, which reintroduces a relay/cost. Primary: RFC 8831 https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8831 , DCEP RFC 8832 https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8832 , ICE RFC 8445 https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8445 , TURN RFC 8656 https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8656 , WebRTC security RFC 8827 https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8827 .
- WebTransport — defer. Attractive server-client multiplexed bidirectional/unidirectional streams plus unreliable datagrams and QUIC migration, but it is not browser-to-browser; does not remove relay/auth/state service; UDP can be blocked; WebTransport-over-HTTP/3 remains an IETF Internet-Draft and W3C calls its API preliminary. Keep an internal transport adapter if later needed, but do not pay deployment/compatibility complexity for tiny control frames. Primary: current H3 draft https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-webtrans-http3 , W3C API https://w3c.github.io/webtransport/ , HTTP/3 UDP fallback warning RFC 9114 section 3.1 https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9114#section-3.1 , QUIC RFC 9000 https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9000 . Important correction: RFC 9297 is HTTP Datagrams and RFC 9298 is CONNECT-UDP; neither is the WebTransport-over-H3 specification.
- BroadcastChannel — local optimization only. Its scope is browsing contexts/workers on the same origin and storage partition/device; no discovery, authentication, NAT traversal, delivery persistence, or cross-origin/device reach. Separate presenter/display origins intentionally prevent it from crossing the security boundary. Primary: WHATWG HTML https://html.spec.whatwg.org/dev/web-messaging.html#broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts .

LAN/cloud conclusion:
- Cloud WSS works across different networks/NAT because each browser establishes an outbound connection; no inbound listener and no peer candidate exchange.
- Optional WebRTC can try host/server-reflexive candidates on LAN and TURN when direct paths fail, but is not MVP.
- Never automatically downgrade to `ws://` local IP. Trusted local TLS relay/certificate provisioning is a distinct offline product.
- WSS remains functional if UDP is blocked, while WebRTC direct paths/WebTransport may fail or relay/fallback.

Acceptance/security gates:
- DISPLAY-role end-to-end capture with seeded private canary: zero private bytes over HTTP/WSS/any future RTC; private subscribe returns TOPIC_FORBIDDEN.
- Evil Origin WSS upgrade with valid cookie: 403.
- Two simultaneous pair redeems: exactly one success; expired, replayed, wrong-account/deck all fail.
- Duplicate/out-of-order/reconnected commands: exactly one authoritative transition; gaps force snapshot.
- Takeover: old socket and queued old epoch can never mutate state.
- Block UDP: presentation control remains green through WSS.
- Slow consumer/oversized messages: bounded memory, state coalescing, policy close; private data absent from errors/logs.

Dead ends closed:
- Anonymous pairing: out of MVP; no display-local SAS flow needed now. QR secret plus existing account/deck authorization is sufficient and avoids an audience race granting authority.
- Cloud-operator E2EE: out of MVP; do not imply WSS is E2EE against the service. Revisit only if operator confidentiality becomes a requirement.
- Fully offline LAN: out of MVP; no insecure local fallback.
- Silent last-writer or last-connection-wins takeover: rejected due accidental/hijacked control.
- Display approval for normal takeover: rejected for MVP because public screen is not a private authorization surface; owner re-auth is recovery.
- WebRTC as mandatory baseline: rejected because signaling + TURN fallback + relay authority remain.
- WebTransport as MVP baseline: rejected due no peer benefit, UDP blocking and still-evolving spec/API.
- BroadcastChannel as second-device transport: impossible by scope.
- Durable bearer/session token in QR, WebSocket query string or localStorage: rejected. Only the constrained one-use pair secret appears in fragment; the durable authenticated session is HttpOnly cookie.

Primary authentication/security references: origin model RFC 6454 https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6454 ; URI fragment RFC 3986 section 3.5 https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3986#section-3.5 ; device-flow security precedent RFC 8628 section 5 https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8628#section-5 ; OAuth Security BCP sender/audience restriction concepts RFC 9700 https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9700 ; host cookie prefix current HTTPbis draft https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-httpbis-rfc6265bis#section-4.1.3.2 .

## EXPAND
none — all raised MVP decision forks are closed by the lead-provided assumptions; remaining WebRTC/WebTransport/offline/E2EE work is explicitly post-MVP and telemetry/requirements-triggered.
summary: Final MVP pairing, takeover, and transport recommendation
